title: v2 pipeline core buildout: cooldown, vision_analyzer, listener, telegram_formatter, vehicle_matcher, tests
author: Jill
trigger: Operator said (2026-09-06, verbatim): "I want you to write a full PrD for this and write the story small enough that they're gonna be able to be done by local model via a specialist and kanban". v2 scaffold + 4 vision prompts already shipped (Phase A, A+, B). The pipeline that consumes them does not exist. Listener is offline in maintenance mode (plist .disabled-20260906-1117stripdown).
background: v2 has 8 infra modules lifted from the old refactor (byte-identical) plus 4 fresh vision prompts (vm1_prompt, vehicle_prompt, person_prompt, animal_prompt) plus the v2 PLAN.md spec. The 11-stage linear pipeline described in PLAN.md is not yet wired. Missing: a pipeline cooldown keyed on (camera_id, classification), a vision analyzer that calls Qwen with the 4 prompts and dispatches by MODE_NAME, three telegram formatter stages (alert, detail, match), a vehicle matcher that consumes VM2 output, the listener pipeline + webhook entrypoint, and tests. Without these, the 4 prompts are unused code. Stories must be small enough for ONE local-qwen specialist pass (validated 2026-09-04: stories >100 LOC crash at ~132k prompt tokens; the cap is ~110k).
goal: Land all 11 stages of v2 pipeline so an end-to-end webhook on CAM1 (or any test camera) routes through cooldown -> gate -> VM1 -> TG#1 -> VM2 -> TG#2 -> match -> TG#3 and reaches Telegram with no operator hand-holding. Tests net-NEGATIVE relative to any lifted baseline (operator rule: tests should go DOWN as we simplify).
non_goals: Do NOT touch /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-refactor/ or /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-internal/. They are frozen archives.
Do NOT touch /tmp/. Build lives at /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2/.
Do NOT bounce the listener. It is in maintenance mode. v2 listener plist NOT installed.
Do NOT modify .env.example templates. They were authored Phase A.
Do NOT modify the 4 vision prompts (vm1_prompt, vehicle_prompt, person_prompt, animal_prompt). Authored Phase B.

Do NOT modify the 8 lifted infra modules (cooldown, gate_cooldown, frame_diff, classify_schema, quick_classifier, vision_cache, motion_types, gate) or the 4 vehicle_position modules. They are byte-identical to the old refactor.
Do NOT git push. Operator reviews and pushes.
Do NOT install new skills. Use the existing skill set.
Do NOT fan out two concurrent coder workers. Single-specialist queue, one story at a time.
Do NOT write ThreatLevel/TG-threat-level fields. Operator 2026-09-06: NO threat-level anywhere.
Do NOT add per-class pipeline modules (vehicle_pipeline/, etc.). Operator 2026-09-06: ONE listener/pipeline.py, no per-class dispatch.
constraints: Each story targets <=100 LOC new code; 150 absolute max. Split before authoring if larger.
Each card body <=2500 chars (Qwen 35B context ceiling after AGENTS.md auto-inject).
Sequential dependency chain via hermes kanban link. Only the head of the chain is in `ready`. No parallel dispatch.
Each AC is a shell-runnable command (grep -nE / python3 -c / python3 -m py_compile / pytest). No prose ACs.
Each story ends with `python3 -m pytest tests/ -x --tb=short` returning baseline-or-better test count. No regression acceptance criterion, no green light.

Worker self-completion bypasses qa/reviewer (validated 2026-09-04 pattern). Operator side: after each `kanban runs <id>` showing 1 run, manually re-dispatch via `hermes kanban request-review --reviewer qa --summary "auto: single-run completion"`.
Tests net-NEGATIVE relative to any lifted baseline. No TestXxxLegacy markers. No commented-out tests. No 'safety net' tests for deleted behavior.
All new code is ASCII only. No Unicode, no em-dashes.
Pre-dispatch gate: confirm `qwen-local :8093` reports 4+ slots. Currently confirmed (llama-server -np 4).
After dispatch, STOP parallel tool calls until worker emits first assistant turn (validated 2026-09-05 starvation pattern).
test_strategy: Per-story `pytest tests/ -x --tb=short` with `pytest --co -q` for collection check. Tests live in `tests/` (empty, must be created in US-013). Project baseline: 0 tests. Net-negative is impossible from 0; the rule becomes 'do not regress to non-zero' — US-013 lands <=20 tests covering pipeline_cooldown + vision_analyzer dispatch + telegram_formatter pure functions + listener webhook routing. Each story that adds logic adds 1-3 tests. Stories that only move code add zero tests.
shipping_definition: Operator sends a synthetic webhook (CAM1, vehicle label, 4 frames already on disk in tests/data/cam1/). pipeline.run() returns within 30s, listener handles the webhook, TG#1 fires with full image + pairwise-diff composite + 4-frame positions, VM2 fires for vehicle with the 2 crops, TG#2 fires with the 2 crops + VM2 output (no threat-level), vehicle_matcher matches the alert, TG#3 fires with the match result. All Telegram messages visible in the operator's chat 374999219. Listener remains offline in production (plist .disabled-20260906-1117stripdown) — the test fixture replays the webhook via `tests/integration/test_end_to_end_pipeline.py::test_synthetic_webhook_reaches_telegram_format` without ever opening the production port. Failure mode: any stage throws an exception, OR TG#1/TG#2/TG#3 silently skipped, OR VM2 output not in the Telegram message body, OR Telegram sends but pytest fails on `mock_telegram.assert_called_once()`.
related: infra/vehicle_prompt.py / person_prompt.py / animal_prompt.py (US-003 depends on these)

stories.title: vehicle_matcher/match.py — pure vehicle matcher
stories.description: vehicle_matcher/__init__.py (empty) + vehicle_matcher/match.py. Function match_vehicle(vm2_result: dict, candidates: list[dict]) -> dict. Takes the VM2 vehicle output + a list of {license_plate, distinctive_features} candidate dicts. Returns the matched candidate dict or {matched: False}. Uses license_plate text first (exact match, case-insensitive, strip whitespace). On no plate or no plate match, falls back to distinctive_features Jaccard >= 0.5. NO file I/O. NO database. Pure function. The actual list of candidates comes from a future story (US-009) that wires the data/vehicles/ store; this story only builds the matcher.

stories.title: listener/pipeline.py::run() — 11-stage linear function
stories.description: listener/__init__.py (empty) + listener/pipeline.py. ONE function run(alert: dict) -> dict. Stages: 1) extract camera_id + classification from alert, 2) cooldown check via PipelineCooldown.should_suppress (drop on True), 3) load 4 frames via vehicle_position, 4) run infra.gate (YOLO gate), 5) drop if gate returns no_surveillance, 6) record_hit on PipelineCooldown (key=classification), 7) call verify_class, 8) build TG#1 via telegram_formatter.alert, 9) call detail_class with the right mode, 10) build TG#2 via telegram_formatter.detail, 11) match vehicle + build TG#3. Returns the dict of {tg1, tg2, tg3}. NO ThreatLevel/TG-threat-level fields anywhere. NO per-class dispatch (no if mode == 'vehicle' branches that import vehicle-only modules). Listener/pipeline.py is the spine.

stories.title: listener/listener.py::handle_webhook() — webhook entrypoint
stories.description: listener/listener.py. Function handle_webhook(alert: dict) -> dict. Wraps pipeline.run() with try/except that returns {'status': 'error', 'stage': str(exc), 'alert_id': alert.get('id')} on any exception. Also handles the Telegram send side: takes the dict returned by pipeline.run() and dispatches tg1/tg2/tg3 to the Telegram client (use python-telegram-bot sync, from env TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN + TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID). The send is wrapped in another try/except so a Telegram failure does not crash the webhook. NO daemonization. NO Flask app. handle_webhook is a plain function; the daemon that calls it is the next story.
acceptanceCriteria: python3 -c "from listener.listener import handle_webhook; print(handle_webhook.__name__)" exits 0
